White Sox catcher Kyle Teel to begin rehab assignment on Tuesday

by Joe Binder August 23, 2026
written by Joe Binder August 23, 2026 2 minutes read
0 comments FacebookTwitterPinterestLinkedinTumblrRedditEmail
424

Kyle Teel has once again been cleared to return to game action.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:33
Instaread

The White Sox announced on Sunday that their starting catcher will begin a rehab assignment with the Charlotte Knights when the affiliate plays next on Tuesday. The news came after Teel successfully ran the bases without issues before the South Siders’ series finale vs. the Mets.

Teel, 24, has had a difficult time staying healthy this season. He initially missed the start of the year after suffering a right hamstring strain on March 10 while playing for Team Italy in the World Baseball Classic. Then, during his first rehab assignment, he sustained a sprained lateral collateral ligament in his right knee on May 16 and was transferred to the 60-day injured list three days later.

After finally making his season debut on June 22, Teel appeared in just under a month’s worth of games where he hit .190/.271/.317 with two homers and 14 RBI. Before he could fully get going offensively, he suffered another setback in the form of a non-contact leg injury against the Rangers on July 20. He went down in considerable pain after twisting his body in an attempt to get the sliding runner and had to be helped off the field. The injury was later diagnosed as a left ankle sprain, with an early September return still appearing to be a realistic possibility.

Since Teel went down, the White Sox have been forced to cycle through a revolving door of catchers. Drew Romo has continued to handle much of the workload, initially alongside Edgar Quero, before the club acquired Joey Bart at the trade deadline. Bart’s stint with the White Sox lasted just three games, however, as he suffered a fractured fifth metacarpal after being hit by a pitch. The team most recently added veteran Jake Rogers to the mix, who came up clutch on Friday night for the team’s 10th walk-off win of the season. Despite some of the individual highlights sprinkled in, the catching position has been anything but the position of strength the White Sox envisioned it to be at the start of the year.

With just a week to go until the calendar flips to the final month of the regular season, the White Sox remain hopeful that Teel can not only return to full health but also provide some much-needed stability behind the plate during their final push toward their first AL Central title since 2021.
